description: The European Union was born from a pragmatic idea: to make the Franco-German war materially impossible by linking coal and steel. Small steps from **1950** in Maastricht.

hero.hook: Make war impossible… by sharing coal and steel.

blocks.text: The **European Union** was not born from a great constitutional evening. She moves forward in “small steps”. In the rubble of 1945, the objective was precise: to make a new war between France and Germany not only unthinkable, but materially impossible.

From the industrial solidarity of **1950** to the political and monetary union of **1992**, Europe is inventing an integration unique in the world. The  becomes the engine. [[Franco-German reconciliation]]

At the end of the war, control of the Ruhr, the great German industrial basin, crystallized tensions. **Jean Monnet**, senior French civil servant, and **Robert Schuman**, Minister of Foreign Affairs, propose a simple idea. **May 9, 1950**, during the , they want to place Franco-German production of coal and steel under a common . [[Schuman Declaration]] [[High Authority]]

blocks.caption: Jean Monnet and Robert Schuman, architects of the first European steps.

blocks.text: Schuman kept his plan so secret that his own diplomats only discovered it on the morning of the announcement.

Coal and steel: the nerves of any arms industry. In **1951**, the **CECA**, European Coal and Steel Community, was born. Italy and the Benelux (Belgium, Netherlands, Luxembourg) join it. For the first time, States are delegating a part of sovereignty to an authority that goes beyond them.

On **March 25, 1957**, the Six signed in Rome the treaties which created the **EEC**, European Economic Community, and the **Euratom** for the civil atom. Objective: a  without customs barriers, based on  (goods, people, services, capital). [[common market]] [[The four freedoms of the common market]]

blocks.caption: Signature of the Treaties of Rome, March 25, 1957.

blocks.text: In Rome, official treaties were not ready in time. For the photo, the leaders signed… blank pages.

In **1962**, the , Common Agricultural Policy, structures agriculture. In **1973**, the United Kingdom, Ireland and Denmark joined the club. From a small industrial circle, the EEC became a commercial power facing the USA and the USSR. [[CAP]]

After 1989 and the fall of the Berlin Wall, to anchor a reunified Germany, integration accelerated. The  transforms the EEC into **European Union**: European citizenship, common foreign policy, economic and monetary union. [[The Treaty of Maastricht (1992)]]

blocks.caption: Franco-German reconciliation, the lasting engine of Europe.

blocks.text: The **euro** became a scriptural reality in 1999, then notes and coins on **January 1, 2002**. The big market now has a currency. But States must also accept common budgetary discipline, a source of future tensions.

In the 2000s, the EU included the former Eastern Bloc countries (28 members in 2013). The Lisbon Treaty reforms the institutions. Then comes the shock: the **Brexit** (2016 vote, 2020 exit). The EU remains a hybrid construction, more than an organization, less than a state.
